title: Streamline legacy flag transport paths and GC orphaned rollout nodes
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: Over time the flag transport layer accumulated multiple routing paths and small compatibility shims used for old rollout formats. These cause: extra serialization work at runtime, confusing admin UI listings, and occasional failures during cross-region failover. Scope: create a safe migration that compacts active flag transport manifests into a canonical path, identifies and garbage-collects orphaned rollout graph nodes, and removes the runtime branching logic that selects deprecated transport formats. Non-goals: changing rollout semantics, migrating customer-facing flag names, or touching historical audit logs (we will snapshot but not rewrite them).
acceptance_criteria: Automated inventory lists all transport variants and marks active vs stale
Migration tool can perform dry-run and produce diff artifacts for each workspace
Canary rollout (5% of traffic) using migrated manifests shows no >5% increase in p95 latency or >1% error delta
Orphaned rollout nodes are removed and associated admin UI entries are cleaned up
All removed runtime branches behind the FEATURE_FLAG_LEGACY_TRANSPORT are deleted and code coverage shows tests passing
Confluence runbook updated and a post-migration incident playbook exists
tasks: Inventory: query routing manifests and admin flag registry; surface transport variants
Add telemetry: migration-diff metrics, sample size histogram, and rollback signals
Run dry-run across staging and gather diffs for team review
Canary migration to 5% production routing in region-us-east-1
Monitor perf and error dashboards for 72 hours, collect traces for any regressions
Full migration, then remove legacy code paths and admin UI elements
Run DB compaction and remove obsolete indexes; update infra migrations
Publish post-mortem and docs; schedule follow-up cleanup sprint if needed
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: silent behavior changes for edge-case rollout graphs. Mitigation: conservative dry-run and canary, track discrepancy metrics
Risk: migration tool accidentally rewrites active manifests. Mitigation: default dry-run, require explicit --commit and a two-person approval gate
Risk: increased latency during canary. Mitigation: scale canary workers and auto-fallback if p95 regression detected
Risk: accidental deletion of audit traces. Mitigation: snapshot audit logs to S3 retention bucket before any destructive steps
notes: Design review 2026-03-02: Agree to canonical transport format (versioned protobuf) and avoid JSON ad-hoc variants
Decision: Keep a short-lived compatibility adapter for legacy mobile clients; deprecate it after 8 weeks
Performance baseline: current p95 token routing latency = 42ms in us-east-1 (metric: routing.latency.p95)
